[2026-10-16; named sparse-Fourier comparison complete]
The NSW sparse-recovery comparison is complete as a conditional norm overlap and qualified model/cost nonmatch. For fixed 0<alpha<1/2 and sufficiently large N, at k=ceil(N^(2alpha)), its spectral-tail error implies the Gaussian N^-alpha ||x||2 scale on its admitted noise/SNR domain, but its explicit cost does not supply the Gaussian bound or rough-padding/covariance construction. Preserve the accepted supporting lemma and F016 obligations. Parent remains TO RESEARCH, priority 12.
